deep.reconstruction:
Setting. A is a small category and Â is its presheaf topos. On Â Grothendieck builds an 'interval' homotopy structure. The cofibrations C are the monomorphisms. TC (the 'trivial cofibrations', i.e. anodyne maps) is generated, as a saturated class, by a small set (TC)_0. This set is built from a bunch of intervals I with endpoint e: roughly the maps (∂x × I) ∪ (x × {e}) → x × I for the boundary inclusions ∂x ⊂ x of representables. F (fibrations) is the class of maps with the RLP with respect to (TC)_0, and TF (trivial fibrations) the class with the RLP with respect to all monomorphisms. W̃ is the class of weak equivalences generated by this data, so that TF = F ∩ W̃ and TC = C ∩ W̃. Condition 2) on an earlier page restricted the intervals so that TC ⊂ W. The aim is to compare W̃ with a given class W of weak equivalences, hoping W̃ = W so that (C, W, F) is a closed model structure.

Argument on this page.
(1) To make W̃ large enough (TC large enough), one needs the bunch of I's to be large enough. The natural condition is that it contains a separating interval (e0, e1 : e → I with e0 ∩ e1 = ∅). Eligible ones are already known: W-aspheric separating intervals, and intervals such as L, the Lawvere interval (subobject classifier).
(2) Take f ∈ W and factor it in either of two ways:
- f = p∘i with i ∈ TC and p ∈ F. Since TC ⊂ W, two-out-of-three gives p ∈ F ∩ W.
- f = p∘i with i ∈ C and p ∈ TF. Since TF ⊂ W, two-out-of-three gives i ∈ C ∩ W.
(3) So W ⊂ W̃ reduces to either inclusion F ∩ W ⊂ TF or C ∩ W ⊂ TC. Each is equivalent to W ⊂ W̃ (i.e. W ∩ W̃ = W), using TF = F ∩ W̃ and TC = C ∩ W̃.
(4) Spelled out, F ∩ W ⊂ TF says: if f ∈ W has the RLP with respect to the generating anodyne maps (TC)_0, then f has the RLP with respect to all monomorphisms. Grothendieck writes 'the second means' but adds '[first?]' above the line; the stated property is indeed the first inclusion.
(5) He wants this at least in two cases.
- (a) W = W_A, where W is a basic localizer and A is a (local?) W-test category. This is the model structure on Â with monomorphisms as cofibrations and W_A as weak equivalences.
- (b) A = A0 × T with T a test category, so Â ≃ Hom(A0^op, T^) ≃ (A0 × T)^. Here W = W_{A/A0} is defined componentwise via W_T, i.e. objectwise weak equivalences of A0-indexed diagrams of T-presheaves.

Case (b) is the 'stacks' motivation of the dossier. It asks for an injective-type model structure on presheaves on A0 with values in a test-category model of homotopy types.
errors: The text says 'The second means ...' but the property described (f ∈ W with RLP w.r.t. (TC)_0 implies RLP w.r.t. all monomorphisms) is the first inclusion F∩W ⊂ TF. Grothendieck himself flags this with '[first?]'.

Equivalence of each inclusion with W ⊂ W̃ uses TF = F∩W̃ and TC = C∩W̃. The first is stated; the second presupposes that the interval structure already behaves like a model structure (retract argument). This is a minor implicit step, not a real gap.
Nothing on the page proves the needed inclusion. It is an open reduction, which Cisinski's later theory resolves in both cases.

ideas.what: Model structure on a presheaf topos with cofibrations = monomorphisms, generated by an interval and a set of generating anodyne maps; F = RLP w.r.t. generators, TF = RLP w.r.t. all monos
ideas.modern_name: Cisinski model structures (homotopical data on Â, Cisinski's 'cylindres' and anodyne extensions)
ideas.usually_credited_to: D.-C. Cisinski (thesis 2002; Astérisque 308, 2006), building on Grothendieck's Pursuing Stacks
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks (1983), sections on 'model structures' on Â and separating intervals

ideas.what: Separating intervals, W-aspheric intervals, and the Lawvere interval L as 'eligible' intervals
ideas.modern_name: Separating segment / Lawvere cylinder from the subobject classifier
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Pursuing Stacks); used systematically by Cisinski

ideas.what: Reduction of W ⊂ W̃ to F∩W ⊂ TF or C∩W ⊂ TC via the two factorizations and 2-out-of-3
Case (a): W_A for a (local) W-test category A gives a closed model structure on Â with monos as cofibrations
ideas.usually_credited_to: Conjectured by Grothendieck (Pursuing Stacks), proved by Cisinski (2002/2006)

ideas.what: Case (b): A = A0 × T, Â ≃ presheaves on A0 valued in T^, with objectwise ('componentwise') weak equivalences W_{A/A0}
ideas.modern_name: Injective (objectwise) model structure on diagrams/presheaves of 'spaces' modelled by a test category; relative localizers W_{A/A0}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Joyal (letter to Grothendieck, 1984; simplicial sheaves), Heller (1988), Jardine (1987); general accessible-localizer version by Cisinski
ideas.where_published: Possibly hinted in Pursuing Stacks / Les Dérivateurs (relative localizers); not stated in this form to my knowledge

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly targets an injective-type model structure (monos as cofibrations, objectwise weak equivalences) on presheaves over a base A0 with values in T-presheaves, T an arbitrary test category. He motivates it by stacks. This anticipates the Joyal–Jardine–Heller injective model structures, generalized from simplicial sets to arbitrary test categories, in the stacks context.
missed.quote: b) A = A0×T, with T a test category, W = W_{A/A0} ... W_{A/A0} is defined componentwise via W_T
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical. It shows Grothendieck's own route to homotopical stacks went through test-category models of diagrams rather than simplicial presheaves. The mathematics is now covered by Cisinski's accessible-localizer theorem.

missed.claim: This is dating evidence that the test-category / basic-localizer / model-structure program was being pursued in the 'Champs' notes. The reused printout paper dates from June 1982, so the page is no earlier than that, possibly before or alongside Pursuing Stacks.
missed.quote: W = W_A (W a basic localizer), A a (local?) W-test category
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Helps the chronology of Pursuing Stacks versus the stacks manuscripts. The paper date is only a lower bound.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is essentially the Pursuing Stacks conjecture later proved by Cisinski, plus a relative/objectwise variant that is now standard. It is mildly interesting as an explicit stacks-motivated formulation and for dating, but there is no new result.
transcription_corrections: The interlinear insertion 'Â ≃ Hom(A0^op, T^) ≃ (A0×T)^' belongs to case (b), not case (a). It is written above line a) but refers to A = A0×T.
'(TC)_0 i.e. all ∂(I_x^i, I, e)' is probably a description of the generating anodyne maps built from boundary inclusions ∂x→x, the interval I and endpoint e. The exact notation is uncertain.
'then it has the RLP more [? ? ? ?] which are in W' likely reads 'then it has the RLP w.r.t. [...] which are in C∩W', later replaced by 'with respect to all monomorphisms'.
Bottom-left margin probably reads 'In both cases Â = A^' (presheaf notation), not 'cA=A^'.
'(or equivalently W∩W̃ = W)': a struck-out symbol precedes W∩W̃.
